notes:
User is looking for high-quality, durable sandals with sturdy straps and is interested in checking out the latest collections from Teva and Merrell. Other suggested durable/comfortable sandal brands include Birkenstock, Sanuk, and Keen; suggested retailers include REI, DSW, Zappos, and Amazon. They have not indicated a purchase beyond checking these options.

User plans to organize their closet this weekend. Old sneakers currently stored under the bed or in a shoe rack are taking up space and may be cleaned, polished, conditioned, repaired, deodorized, or evaluated for donation. They plan to take the sneakers to a cobbler this weekend and will look for a reliable local provider through recommendations from friends/family and online reviews, or consider reputable mail-in services. Before storage, they want to keep sneakers clean and fresh: clean and fully dry them, maintain their shape with shoe trees or stuffing, use odor absorbers, ensure ventilation, avoid direct sun/heat/dampness, protect them from dust and scratches, and check periodically for mold or mildew.

User plans to donate old dress shoes to a local charity thrift store this Saturday. They will call ahead and check the charity’s website/guidelines first. Shoes should be clean, polished, wearable, and free of major damage; heavily worn soles, cracked uppers, broken heels, torn seams, or unwearable shoes may be rejected. Alternatives include another charity, repurposing, or a shoe-recycling program.

User also plans to inventory and declutter their shoe collection, including checking for forgotten pairs in the closet. They may donate, sell, repair, recycle, or repurpose shoes that are unworn, duplicated, damaged, or no longer useful. They are considering organizing shoes by type (boots together, sneakers together, etc.) and may use dividers, stackable shoe racks or shelves, bins/baskets, vertical space, and separate storage for out-of-season shoes while keeping frequently worn pairs accessible. Over-the-door organizers may also save space.

User jogs regularly and wants a change of scenery from the same route they have used for months. They have not provided a location, so no specific nearby route can be recommended. Potential discovery methods include Google Maps, local Parks and Recreation departments, MapMyRun, Runkeeper, Strava, asking friends/family/coworkers, and exploring rail trails, canal paths, parks, or nature reserves. Prioritize daylight/reflective gear, hydration, situational awareness, and telling someone the planned route and return time.
